subject.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this folder-backed encrypted snapshot flow with new backup config now, or should the native scope be narrowed while broader cloud/scheduled backup behavior stays in plugin or ClawHub territory?
rationale: The PR adds destructive restore behavior, new config surface, encrypted storage, workspace mirroring, and backup target policy, so maintainers need to choose the first-party backup boundary separately from code-level fixes.

options.title: Narrow Core Restore First
options.body: Define and land a minimal core restore/snapshot contract with strict path safety, rollback, docs, and real CLI proof before expanding backup targets or scheduling semantics.

options.title: Defer Folder Snapshots Outside Core
options.body: Keep core on local archive create/verify for now and route folder/cloud snapshot automation through a plugin or ClawHub package unless missing core APIs are identified.

options.title: Sponsor Full Core Backup Platform
options.body: Accept the broader core direction, but require a maintainer-owned design for encryption, retention, restore drills, migrations, and upgrade compatibility before merge.

recommendation.title: Narrow Core Restore First
recommendation.body: Define and land a minimal core restore/snapshot contract with strict path safety, rollback, docs, and real CLI proof before expanding backup targets or scheduling semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans product scope, ClawHub/plugin routing, and security-sensitive restore policy rather than one local code owner decision.
